newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends down on speculative selling.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends down on speculative selling.

text.p: NEW YORK, Feb 10 Reuter) - NYCE cotton futures settled lower after speculators, disappointed by the market's failure to hold early gains, began to sell in the afternoon, dealers said.
Losses accelerated once stops were triggered below 74.25 cents a lb in March delivery, they added. The contract closed barely above support at 74.00 cents and then at 73.30 cents.
March settled down 0.32 cent at 74.26 cents after trading from 75.00 to 73.95 cents. The back months ended 0.25 to 0.05 weaker.
Analysts said the market could rack up gains Wednesday when USDA releases its monthly supply and demand data.
They said the recent brisk sales, coupled with shrinking supplies overseas, will prompt USDA to raise its export forecast to between 6.4 million and 6.6 million 480-lb bales from 6.3 million bales.
Estimates for U.S. output and domestic consumption are expected to be unchanged at 18.95 million bales and 11.0 million bales, respectively.
